MONTE CARLO FLIPPED DECISIVELY UP-FIRST: adjusted prob_up_first jumped to 64.5% (from ~39% down-first prior) with median days upside 2d vs downside 5d — the strongest up-skew of the recovery, though it still just misses the 70% Late Bull threshold.

VALUATION REMAINS PINNED AT THE CEILING: 10-year eased to 4.539% but ERP is only ~0.0% (0.0042) against forward PE 20.17x — the thinnest possible cushion, keeping trim bias fully active.

BREADTH STILL NON-CONFIRMING: McClellan Summation at 929.86 (score 24) sits near its lower band and 52-week highs/lows strength only 2.33 (score 43) — participation has not validated the price recovery.
narrative_summary: SPX closed 7,543.64 (+0.8%), reclaiming the 23.6% fib and the ERP re-entry floor and pushing within ~0.5% of the June 15 swing high, while the Monte Carlo edge flipped decisively up-first (64.5%) and VIX eased back below 16. But the rally continues to run into a zero-cushion ERP (~0.0%) pinned at the valuation ceiling, breadth (McClellan 930, near its lows) and credit (junk spread 1.31, wide) that still refuse to confirm, and an edge that just misses the 70% Late Bull threshold. The structural bias remains Late Bull / Topping: a mechanically intact, momentum-improving bull skeleton colliding with late-cycle valuation and participation warnings. Trim bias into strength — not chasing the grind into the swing high — remains the justified posture.
